i came into the emergency room today with my significant other and left with a bitter feeling of distastefulness recounting the interaction we had with the staff greeting you as you walked in. 
given the current circumstances, i understand the seriousness and risk involved with visiting the emergency room. it was not a decision that was made light-heartedly. 
as we walked in we were asked what our reason for being there and as we told them they sent us to the registration window. my partner was asked to step aside. as i a stood at the registration window, they continued to ask him general screening questions. "do you have a cough? a fever?" it was evident that we were not there for covid-19 related illnesses, as we had previously told them upon entering the facility. as this was made clear they proceeded to ask, "are you a doctor?" no. "are you a nurse?" no. "then why are you here? don't you know this area is high-risk?" these rhetorical questions were asked to make a mockery of my partner. i have never felt so disrespected and belittled by hospital staff or employees ever. it caught me off guard and made me upset. this is not the way you greet people, especially to those who are simply seeking your help.

on friday, 4/17/2020, my grandma was taken to your medical facility, garfield medical center at around 4:00 pm. my grandma whom has tested positive for covid-19 began presenting worsening symptoms and due to her advanced age, we decided it would be best to take her to the hospital. we chose your facility because of your good reputation, nonetheless, we feel we were let down on this said day. my sister took our grandma in her car, taking a high risk of getting infected herself, for i could not transport her myself because i am also positive for covid-19 as well. we truly believe (my sister, my grandma, my mother, and i) that my grandma was de-serviced on this day. i understand the unique and precarious circumstances we are under does not allow for things to be normal, nonetheless, this does not mean for my grandma to sit in a car for two (2) hours, basically, unattended as my sister has no medical back-ground. the only thing that was done for my grandma was; insurance information, temperature, and basic vitals were taken on her upon arrival while in the car. as a matter of fact, my grandma never left the car for two hours, while waiting in the er parking lot under the assigned area. my sister kept on asking, politely, how much longer before grandma would be taken in, and she was given the runaround a few times. the staff did not take action to take my grandma in, until my sister finally lost some of her patience and composure, and raised her voice to let staff know she was leaving and she was taking grandma elsewhere. it was not until this moment that the staff finally came with a wheelchair and tried to do something trying to justify their delay. my sister stated to them that why did she have to raise her voice to get things done, that was not right, what if she had not raised her voice, how long would she have waited? that is a question my sister was not willing to gamble on with grandma. 
basically, nothing was done for my grandma, and yet, insurance information was taken which leads me to believe we will get billed for having had my grandma sit in her car outside the er for two hours. is this justifiable? consider the fact that none of us are currently working, therefore, income is a very serious issue. what will we get billed for, let me see, for nothing? how will you justify billing us for having had grandma, whom was identified as a senior citizen and positive for covid-19, to just sit in the car, hungry, and with uncertainty? my sister rushed my grandmother to alhambra hospital medical center and they quickly received her and attended to her care.
